_comment: Manifest for scripts/check_dng_ffi_artifacts.py. Data only — adding or flipping a platform must never require editing the checker script. Governance: per-feature preference cascade (C-8/P-1) stands (2026-08-24). RAW decoder ships macOS+Windows+Android today. Linux .so is open item P-2, not a blocker. No iOS entry — iOS FFI is superseded by the future general raw_decoder effort (see plan Dropped section), not part of this manifest.

macos.comment: Vendored arm64 dylib; ruling P-12 confirmed this symbol is exported.

r7.measures: the shipped macOS decoder dylib exists and exposes the sized-decode entry point
r7.why_valid: Mach-O with permissive default visibility: an exported symbol really is reachable via dlopen/dlsym, so the symbol table agrees with the runtime. The functional FFI probe (scripts/ci/probe/ffi_probe.dart) is the primary instrument regardless; nm is a secondary cross-check only.
r7.red_state: point the checker at a dylib built without dng_decode_and_process_sized, or delete the dylib: symbol=absent / present=False and RC=1

macos-x86_64.comment: Intel/x86_64 macOS. SAME on-disk path as the 'macos' entry on purpose: build_apps.py places whichever architecture --macos-arch selected at that one path (fetch_target_for(), build_apps.py:1440-1467), so only ONE of the two can be on disk at a time and the manual checker reads whichever the last build fetched. The CI assertions do NOT read this path -- they read the member inside the built/packaged artefact -- so the shared path is not a source of ambiguity there. expected_arch is what distinguishes this entry: it is the value H-ARCH and H-DECODER-ARCH judge the macos-x64 leg against.

r7.measures: the shipped Intel macOS app and its decoder dylib are both x86_64, and the dylib exposes every ceyx entry point
r7.why_valid: Architecture is read structurally from the Mach-O header in pure Python, which is host-independent, and nm parses a foreign-architecture Mach-O file on any host -- both instruments therefore stay valid on the Apple-silicon runner that cross-compiles this leg. The functional FFI probe does NOT: an arm64 process cannot dlopen an x86_64 dylib, so H-SIZED-SYMBOL is omitted from this target's assertion list in scripts/ci/targets.py, visibly and in data. A green macos-x64 leg consequently claims correct bytes, NOT demonstrated runtime loadability on Intel hardware.
r7.red_state: fetch the macos-arm64 pin entry for this leg (or build without --macos-arch x86_64): H-DECODER-ARCH / H-ARCH fail naming expected x86_64 vs observed arm64
r7.expected: present=True, arch=x86_64 for both the app executable and the decoder, and all of dng_decode_and_process_sized / ceyx_probe_output_size / ceyx_decode_into_buffer listed by nm

windows.comment: Trust-on-first-use: built on a real Windows host (commit d36e1bd) but no S4 colour-gate run recorded. dumpbin is unavailable on non-Windows hosts, so this platform legitimately reports symbol=skipped when checked from macOS/Linux.

r7.measures: the shipped Windows decoder DLL exists alongside its two dynamic imports
r7.why_valid: Presence and architecture of a PE file are read structurally (IMAGE_FILE_HEADER.Machine), which is format-defined and host-independent. The SYMBOL-TABLE half is NOT claimed valid here: PE exports nothing by default, so dumpbin /exports measures a build-system setting rather than runtime reachability (ceyx 2026-08-30). Runtime reachability on Windows is measured only by the functional FFI probe, and only on a Windows host.
r7.red_state: delete dng_decoder_native.dll from a staging copy: present=False and RC=1. The dumpbin symbol half has NO demonstrated red state on this machine — see PL-9.
r7.expected: present=True; symbol=skipped when inspected from a non-Windows host

r7.measures: the arm64-v8a decoder shared object exists and exports the sized-decode entry point
r7.why_valid: ELF dynamic symbol table with default visibility: nm -D lists exactly what dlsym can resolve. No CI assertion consumes this entry — the android-apk target declares no R-7 assertions this round (Plan §6 / PL-5); it stays here for the manual cross-platform checker.
r7.red_state: delete the .so or strip the symbol: present=False / symbol=absent and RC=1

linux.comment: Open item P-2: Linux .so does not exist yet. Flip 'expected' to true the day it lands; no script changes needed.

r7.measures: the shipped Linux decoder shared object exists and exposes the sized-decode entry point
r7.why_valid: ELF dynamic symbol table with default visibility: nm -D lists exactly what dlopen/dlsym can resolve. The functional FFI probe remains the primary instrument; nm is a secondary cross-check.
r7.red_state: delete the .so or point at one built without the symbol: present=False / symbol=absent and RC=1
r7.expected: expected=false today (P-2): absent is not a failure until the .so lands
